tasks.title: Add the task file's two lifecycle times

- a file written before this release has neither key, loads, and saves without gaining them
tasks.closed_reason:
- TaskFile gains optional bound_at and imported_at (*time.Time, omitempty, RFC 3339) in internal/model/taskfile.go; TestReadWriteTaskFile_LifecycleTimesRoundTrip reads and writes both unchanged
- A file without either key loads and saves without gaining them: TestReadWriteTaskFile_OldFileGainsNoLifecycleTimes (internal/model/io_test.go); gate passed

tasks.title: Stamp bound_at when the binding changes
tasks.description: tp init --epic and tp set --epic write bound_at only when the file's epic changes; tp set --epic "" removes it with epic.
tasks.acceptance:
- `tp set --epic E1` on an unbound file writes `bound_at`; `tp init <spec> --epic E1` writes it on the new file
- §18 row 11: a file bound to a, re-bound to a (bound_at unchanged), then to b (bound_at moves); the mutant writing a stamp on every `set --epic` turns it red
- `tp set --epic ""` removes `bound_at` together with `epic`
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp set --epic a on an unbound file writes bound_at in UTC (applyEpicBinding in internal/cli/set_epic.go) and tp init <spec> --epic a writes it on the new file (boundAtFor in internal/cli/init.go); an unbound init writes none: TestSetEpic_BoundAtMovesOnlyWhenTheEpicChanges, TestInit_EpicWritesBoundAt
- §18 row 11 fixture (bound to a, re-bound to a, then to b): bound_at unchanged on the re-bind and later after b; the mutant stamping on every set --epic turns TestSetEpic_BoundAtMovesOnlyWhenTheEpicChanges red at the re-bind
- tp set --epic "" removes bound_at with epic: TestSetEpic_EmptyRemovesBoundAtWithTheEpic, red under the mutant that keeps a stamp on removal; gate passed

tasks.title: Stamp imported_at on every import
tasks.description: tp import writes imported_at and rewrites it on every later import into the file, --force included.
tasks.acceptance:

- a file imported before this release loads with no `imported_at` and nothing reports a time for it
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp import stamps imported_at (UTC) just before its write, so every import into the file, --force included, moves it (internal/cli/importcmd.go): TestImport_WritesImportedAtAndEveryImportMovesIt; the mutant skipping the stamp under --force turns it red (second imported_at nil)
- A file written before the release has no imported_at and a non-import write (tp claim) adds none: TestImport_FileImportedBeforeTheReleaseGainsNoImportedAt (internal/cli/import_imported_at_test.go); the mutant stamping in model.WriteTaskFile on every write turns it red; gate passed

tasks.title: Match thresholds against the placeholder pattern
tasks.description: Engine: one function giving the placeholder verdict for a gate threshold under the default pattern or a project pattern that replaces it.
tasks.acceptance:
- default pattern: a trimmed threshold wholly inside one pair of square or angle brackets, or `TBD`, `TODO`, `TBC` alone in any case, is a placeholder; `draft: 80% pass` and written text are not
- a project pattern replaces the default: under `^draft:` the text `draft: 80% pass` matches and `[threshold]` and `TBD` do not
- an absent or empty threshold is never a placeholder
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.NewPlaceholderMatcher(pattern) with (*PlaceholderMatcher).IsPlaceholder(threshold) (internal/engine/placeholder.go; names chosen); the default, engine.DefaultThresholdPlaceholder, is (?i)^(?:\[[^\[\]]*\]|<[^<>]*>|TBD|TODO|TBC)$ over the trimmed threshold: TestPlaceholderMatcher_DefaultPattern ([threshold], <exit condition>, TBD, todo, Tbc match; draft: 80% pass, [a] and [b], TBD by Friday, written text do not), red before the change (undefined)
- a non-empty project pattern replaces the default (an empty one is the default; one that does not compile returns the compile error, for the config-key task): TestPlaceholderMatcher_AProjectPatternReplacesTheDefault (^draft: matches draft: 80% pass, not [threshold] or TBD); the mutant OR-ing the default beside the project pattern turns it red
- an absent or blank threshold is never a placeholder, even under ^$ or .*: TestPlaceholderMatcher_AnAbsentThresholdIsNeverAPlaceholder; the mutant dropping the blank check turns it red; gate passed

tasks.title: Read epic.threshold_placeholder from the project config
tasks.description: The project config gains epic.threshold_placeholder, one regular expression matched against the trimmed threshold; tp validate --project refuses one that does not compile.
tasks.acceptance:
- `.tp/config.json`'s `epic.threshold_placeholder` is the pattern the matcher uses; a config without it uses the default
- `tp validate --project` refuses a pattern that does not compile, naming the key and the compile error
- `tp config` shows the key, and `tp config --extract` leaves it intact
tasks.closed_reason:
- .tp/config.json gains a top-level epic block, {threshold_placeholder} (model.ProjectConfig.Epic *EpicProjectConfig, omitempty), parsed leniently by LoadProjectConfig (unknown epic key / non-string value warn and are ignored); engine.ProjectThresholdPlaceholder(tpDir) and engine.ProjectPlaceholderMatcher(tpDir) give the pattern the matcher uses, the default when the key is absent or empty or no .tp/ exists: TestProjectPlaceholderMatcher_UsesTheConfiguredPattern, _WithoutTheKeyUsesTheDefault, TestLoadProjectConfig_AnUnknownOrWrongTypedEpicKeyWarns, red before the change (no field)
- tp validate --project exits 1 (ExitValidation, reading chosen) when the pattern does not compile, the error naming epic.threshold_placeholder and the regexp compile error, with a repair hint; a malformed config stays under skipped as before: TestValidateProject_RefusesAPlaceholderPatternThatDoesNotCompile, red before the change (exit 0)
- tp config prints epic: {threshold_placeholder: <effective pattern, the default when unset>} beside workflow, and --resolved prints it as {value, source} with source project or default (reading chosen); tp config --extract --force keeps the epic block since the model carries it: TestConfig_ShowsTheThresholdPlaceholder, TestConfigExtract_KeepsTheThresholdPlaceholder, both red before the change (no key; the extract dropped epic); gate passed

tasks.title: Add the gate-threshold-unwritten lint rule

tasks.acceptance:

- operator.gates lists a gate only when its members are done and its threshold is written and not a placeholder: engine.WithoutPlaceholderGates filters EpicReady's Gates by the project matcher (internal/engine/epicrewrite.go, epicReadyReport in internal/cli/epic_ready.go); TestEpicOperator_PlaceholderGatesAreListedAsRewritesOnly lists W (done, written) alone, not P (done, TBD); red before the change; the mutant keeping placeholder gates lists P, W and turns it red

tasks.closed_reason:
- .tp/epics.json accepts top-level forbidden_edges, [{from, to, why}] (model.EpicGraph.ForbiddenEdges, omitempty, written after tag_checks; model.EpicForbiddenEdge, model.EpicSelector) and the loader knows the key and the rule keys (internal/engine/epicgraph.go), so version stays 1 and every writer carries it: TestEpicGraph_ForbiddenEdgesAreAcceptedAndCarriedByEveryWriter (lint clean of unknown-key; set, add, link keep the rule; import round-trips the file byte-identically), red before the change (unknown-key); TestEpicGraph_AnUnknownKeyInAForbiddenRuleIsAnUnknownKey reports forbidden_edges[0].owner
- a selector with no key, two keys or a key outside epic, milestone, tag, track_of fails EpicSelector.UnmarshalJSON, so it is refused exactly as a value of the wrong type: tp epic import exits 2 and writes nothing, and every reader of a hand-edited file exits 3 (reading chosen: a type-level schema error, not a new lint rule): TestEpicGraph_AMalformedSelectorIsASchemaError; the mutant decoding the selector as a plain struct turns all three cases red. No tp epic set forbidden_edges= key was added (not in the acceptance); gate passed

tasks.title: Lint forbidden_edges selectors for dangling references
tasks.description: Selector references: a missing epic or milestone is dangling-reference, an uncarried tag a warning, an empty why missing-why.
tasks.acceptance:
- an `epic`, `milestone` or `track_of` selector naming nothing the graph holds is a `dangling-reference` error
- a `tag` no epic carries is a warning, so a rule may precede its tag; a rule without a why is `missing-why`
tasks.closed_reason:
- An epic, milestone or track_of selector of a forbidden_edges rule naming nothing the graph holds is a dangling-reference error, one per selector, message 'forbidden_edges[i].<from|to> <key> "<v>" names no epic|milestone' (lintEpicForbiddenRules in internal/engine/epiclint_forbidden.go, run from LintEpicGraph; Origin DanglingForbiddenRule): TestLintEpicGraph_ForbiddenSelectorsNamingNothingAreDanglingReferences, red before the change; mutants dropping the lint call, or checking track_of against epic ids, turn it red. Writers refuse it like every new error: TestEpicGraph_RemovingAnEpicARuleNamesIsRefused (tp epic remove of the one epic a rule names exits 1, names the selector, carries the new forbidden_edges refusal hint, writes nothing)
- A tag selector no epic carries is a dangling-reference warning (reading chosen: the same rule at warning severity, since the docs task adds no new lint-table row for it), so SummarizeEpicLint counts no error: TestLintEpicGraph_AForbiddenTagNoEpicCarriesIsAWarning, the mutant leaving it an error turns it red; a rule whose why is empty or blank is a missing-why error 'forbidden_edges[i] has no why': TestLintEpicGraph_AForbiddenRuleWithoutAWhyIsMissingWhy; gate passed

tasks.title: Add tp epic review --history for one slice
tasks.description: --history prints the slice's rounds, each with findings by role and the diff from the round before, then the diff from the last round to the current graph; --from/--to narrow it.
tasks.acceptance:
- `tp epic review <slice> --history` prints each recorded round with findings by role and its diff from the round before, then last round to current graph; `--from <a> --to <b>` narrows to those two rounds
- read-only, runs under `TP_UNATTENDED`, exits 3 for a slice with no state directory; `--compact` drops each diff's unchanged context and keeps every change
- a hash-only round reports no edge or why text and says so

tasks.title: Add --history --of-epic across every slice
tasks.description: One epic's edges and whys per recorded round of every slice whose snapshot holds it.
tasks.acceptance:
- `tp epic review --history --of-epic <id>` prints the epic's edges and whys per recorded round of every slice whose snapshot holds it
- a slice with two recorded rounds between which one edge's why was rewritten lists that edge under both rounds
- an epic in no recorded slice reports no graph history and says so

tasks.title: Split a spec into anchored sections
tasks.description: Engine: the spec's text as numbered sections, each section and paragraph with a stable anchor (§3 ¶2).
tasks.acceptance:
- a spec parses into its numbered sections, each paragraph anchored `§N ¶M`
- editing a later section leaves every earlier anchor unchanged; an unnumbered heading gets the anchor rule this task pins
tasks.closed_reason:
- a spec parses into its sections with each paragraph anchored `§N ¶M`: engine.SpecSections(data) returns []SpecSection{anchor, heading, line, paragraphs[{anchor, line, text}]} (internal/engine/specsections.go; type, field and JSON names chosen for the tp export task to publish). §0 is the preamble (its first H1 its heading, left out when empty), a numbered heading of level 2-6 opens §<number> (floorAnchorsByLine's rule, headingNumRe), a paragraph is a run of non-blank lines, a fenced block one paragraph whatever it holds, frontmatter blanked so line numbers count it. TestSpecSections_ParsesNumberedSectionsWithParagraphAnchors and TestSpecSections_FrontmatterIsNotAParagraph; red before the change (undefined SpecSections)
- editing a later section leaves every earlier anchor unchanged, and the pinned rule for an unnumbered heading: an unnumbered level-2 heading opens §<slug> (lowercased, each run of non-letter/digit characters one hyphen), an anchor taken earlier takes the next free suffix (-2, -3) so an anchor depends only on the text above it, and an unnumbered level-3+ heading is a paragraph of its section. TestSpecSections_ALaterEditLeavesEveryEarlierAnchorUnchanged adds a paragraph to §2, a new §3 and a second '## Non-goals' and reads the first 12 anchors unchanged and the new one as §non-goals-2; mutants: no dedup suffix turns it red, positional anchors for unnumbered headings turn both tests red; gate passed
- Coordinator follow-up fix (no task id), commits a4b6923d (fix) and b41b762a (test): tp epic ready, tp epic status and tp epic export no longer exit 3 when .tp/config.json cannot be read or epic.threshold_placeholder does not compile; epicPlaceholderMatcher (internal/cli/epic_ready.go, was epicPlaceholderMatcherOrExit) prints one output.Notice warning on stderr naming epic.threshold_placeholder and falls back to engine.DefaultThresholdPlaceholder; tp validate --project still refuses the pattern. TestEpicReadCommands_FallBackOnAnUncompilablePlaceholder: config pattern '([' -> each of the three commands exits 0, the key appears once on stderr, and ready lists P (TBD) and Q ([threshold]) as rewrites; red on HEAD (exit 3)

tasks.title: Build one task file's export read model
tasks.description: Engine: tasks with their state, each loop with its rounds and snapshot diffs, the tp resume view, the epic and both lifecycle times.
tasks.acceptance:
- every task carries status, dependencies, estimate, acceptance, `source_sections`, times, closing evidence, commits and a state: ready, waits on a task, waits on its epic
- ground, review and audit loops carry cap, clean rounds needed and streak, and per recorded round its time, finding or FAIL count, clean flag and spec-snapshot diff from the round before
- the model carries the `tp resume` view, the epic, `bound_at` and `imported_at`

tasks.title: Add the tp export command
tasks.description: tp export prints the read model of the task file --file names or discovery finds, version 1; --compact drops bulky fields.
tasks.acceptance:
- `tp export --file spec/1.5.0.tasks.json` prints `version`, the sections with anchors, the tasks, the loops with one entry per recorded round and the `tp resume` view
- `--compact` prints no section body, task description or snapshot diff, and compacts the resume view as `tp resume --compact`
- runs under `TP_UNATTENDED`; with no task file, or an unreadable one, it exits 3 with a hint

tasks.title: Add tp export --list over every task file
tasks.description: One row per task file, bound or not, in phase order: path, title, epic and its state, phase, task counts, review and audit rounds, next step, escalation.
tasks.acceptance:
- in tp's own repository it prints one row per `spec/*.tasks.json`, none bound, each under the phase `tp resume <file>` reports, in phase order
- §18 row 10: two task files, one malformed, exit 0 with the readable row kept and the bad one carrying its error; the mutant exiting 3 on the first bad file turns it red
- with no task file it exits 0 with an empty list; `TP_UNATTENDED=1 tp export --list` exits 0

tasks.title: Settle the summary payload with per-round counts
tasks.description: The dashboard summary payload (figures no command prints) is defined here; this task adds per slice each recorded round's finding count, total and by role, in round order.
tasks.acceptance:
- the summary payload's shape (round counts, band, release impact, per-day series) is settled and pinned by a JSON shape test
- for a slice with two recorded rounds the summary carries two per-round entries whose by-role counts sum to each round's total
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.DashboardSummary (internal/engine/dashsummary.go) fixes the summary's four top-level keys per the coordinator's decision (option a): rounds, band, release_impact, series; only rounds is filled, band and release_impact are {} and series is [], and their inner shape is owned by summary-lifecycle-band, summary-release-impact and summary-daily-series, each extending TestDashboardSummary_ShapeIsPinned; mutant series,omitempty turns it red
- rounds maps each slice state directory name (tp epic export's slices[].dir) to [{round, total, by_role}] in round order, every finding counted whatever its disposition, a roleless one under unattributed: TestDashboardSummary_RoundCountsByRoleSumToEachTotal (two rounds: 3 = why-auditor 2 + phase-economist 1, then 1 = unattributed 1); mutant counting only undisposed findings turns it red; gate passed. Also landed before this close, per the coordinator: open_by_role counts a roleless finding under engine.EpicRoleUnattributed (fix fe714bb1, test d1ec5857 TestEpicReviewStatus_CountsARolelessFindingAsUnattributed, red under the former "" key)

tasks.title: Count work epics per stage over phases
tasks.description: Summary band: epic stages over spec phases, counting work epics.
tasks.acceptance:
- the band counts work epics per stage (planned, claimed, specced, in progress, done) and per spec phase; an epic with several bound specs counts once, at its earliest phase
- with no graph the phases count task files; with a graph an unbound task file is not counted
tasks.closed_reason:
- the band counts work epics per stage (planned, claimed, specced, in_progress, done) and per spec phase (review, decompose, implement, audit, release), an epic with several bound specs once at its earliest phase: engine.LifecycleBand(g, states, epicPhases, filePhases) -> DashboardBand{stages, phases, phases_of} (internal/engine/dashband.go; type, keys and phases_of chosen, the dashboard's own payload: both maps always carry every key of their axis, conditions are left out via IsWorkEpic), carried as summary.band by DashboardSummaryOf, which reads it with DashboardBandOf(parent of tpDir, g) (bound files' tp resume phases and DeriveEpicStates). TestLifecycleBand_CountsWorkEpicsPerStageAndEarliestPhase (d bound at audit and implement counts once at implement, condition x in neither axis) reads stages 1/1/1/1/2 and phases review 1, implement 1, release 1; red before the change (undefined); mutants counting every bound file and taking the latest phase each turn it red; TestDashboardSummary_ShapeIsPinned extended to pin band's keys
- with no graph (nil, or a graph with no epics) the phases count task files (every *.tasks.json git sees) and phases_of reads task_files; with a graph an unbound task file is not counted: TestLifecycleBand_WithNoGraphThePhasesCountTaskFiles (review 1, implement 2, every stage 0) and, on a real repository, TestDashboardBandOf_ReadsTheRepositorysTaskFiles (b's bound file and an unbound file, both open: the graph's band counts implement 1, with no graph 2); the pure test's unbound decompose file reads decompose 0 under a graph; gate passed

tasks.title: Derive each spec's release impact on the plan
tasks.description: Summary: per bound spec, the epics releasing it would free and the gate it would move.
tasks.acceptance:
- for a bound spec whose epic is the last undone dependency of another, the impact names that epic as freed and the gate whose done count moves
- an unbound spec carries an empty impact
tasks.closed_reason:
- for a bound spec whose epic is the last undone dependency of another, the impact names that epic as freed and the gate whose done count moves: engine.SpecReleaseImpact(g, states, id) -> ReleaseImpact{frees, gates[{milestone, members_done, members_done_after, members}]} (internal/engine/dashimpact.go; names and shape chosen, the dashboard's own payload), freed = every not-done epic an undone dependency holds now and none would with id done (epicWaitFlags, so any-of groups count), gates = tracked milestones whose gateMembersCount changes; summary.release_impact keys every task file git sees by its repo-relative path, a bound file carrying its epic's impact only when every other file bound to that epic is at release (reading chosen: otherwise its release finishes no epic), read in one pass by the new dashRepo (internal/engine/dashband.go refactor, DashboardSummaryOf). TestSpecReleaseImpact_NamesTheFreedEpicAndTheMovedGate frees b (a its last undone dependency), not d (still waits on x), M1 1->2 of 4, nothing once a is done; TestDashboardSummary_CarriesEachSpecsReleaseImpact on a real repository: b.tasks.json frees a and moves M 2->3 of 4, and is empty once a second spec of b is not at release; red before the change (undefined); mutants freeing every blocked dependent, and ignoring the other bound files, each turn one red; shape test pins the entry keys
- an unbound spec carries an empty impact {frees: [], gates: []}: u.tasks.json in TestDashboardSummary_CarriesEachSpecsReleaseImpact; gate passed

tasks.title: Derive the per-day lifecycle series
tasks.description: Summary: work epics per stage per day from the times tp records, ending at the last recorded event.
tasks.acceptance:
- claimed dates from `claimed.at`, specced from the earliest `bound_at` when every bound file has one (else unknown), in progress from the earliest task `started_at`, done from `done_at`; the series ends at the last recorded event
- an epic claimed, bound and done on three days appears in claimed, specced and done on those days
- §18 row 12: an epic with no `bound_at`, one with it, one with two bound files only one carrying it (unknown); mutants reading `created_at`, or the one file that has it, turn it red

tasks.title: Add the tp dashboard command
tasks.description: tp dashboard [--port N]: binds 127.0.0.1:7377 by default, prints the URL, serves an embedded page until interrupted. Standard library only.
tasks.acceptance:
- in a repository with a graph it prints `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` (7377 unless `--port`), and a GET of it returns the page; a taken port exits 1 naming it
- `TP_UNATTENDED=1` exits 2; §18 row 2: an empty directory exits 3 with a hint, a directory with one task file serves; the mutant requiring a graph turns it red
- after the server has run, `git status` shows no change it made

tasks.title: Serve GET requests from the bound host only
tasks.description: Only GET is served; a Host other than the bound address and port (or localhost with that port) is refused; no CORS header.
tasks.acceptance:
- every method but GET is refused; a `Host` not the bound address and port, nor `localhost` with that port, is refused; no response carries a CORS header
- §18 row 1 (repo with one task file): the listener is on 127.0.0.1 only and a second instance on the port exits 1 naming it; mutants listening on all interfaces, or serving any method, turn it red
- the page, its script and styles are served from the binary's embed

tasks.title: Push changed payloads over Server-Sent Events
tasks.description: A fixed tick re-derives the epic export (when a graph exists), tp export --list and the summary in-process, and pushes each only when its content, generated_at left out, changed.
tasks.acceptance:
- each tick derives the three payloads in-process and pushes one only when its content without `generated_at` changed; a reconnecting client gets the current state
- §18 row 3: graph with one unbound task file, and a task file with no graph, two ticks each: nothing pushed after the first state, a `tp done` reaches the stream; mutants deciding on a payload with `generated_at`, or on the epic export alone, turn it red
- a failing derivation pushes tp's error and hint; a graph added while the server runs is pushed with no restart

tasks.title: Serve read models on demand by GET
tasks.description: GET endpoints for one task file's tp export and a slice's or an epic's graph history, produced in-process by the commands' code.
tasks.acceptance:
- a GET returns one task file's `tp export`, a slice's `--history` and an epic's `--of-epic` history, byte-equal in content to the commands' JSON
- an unknown file or slice answers with tp's error; a path outside the repository is refused

tasks.title: Port the prototype shell with three tabs
tasks.description: Embedded page from the approved prototype (scratchpad dashboard-proto/index.html, v9, synthetic data) rewired to the SSE payloads: Epics, Specs and Spec tabs, no framework, library or CDN.
tasks.acceptance:
- with a graph the page opens on Epics; with task files and no graph it opens on Specs, and the Epics tab names `tp epic` as the way to start a graph and its band shows the spec phases alone
- a pushed error shows as a banner over the last good state, greyed (a hand edit breaking the graph keeps the previous map)
- a Go test asserts the embedded page names the SSE endpoint and the three payloads' event names, and references no `http://` or `https://` resource

tasks.title: Keep the page's place in the URL
tasks.description: Tab, spec, view, task, selected epic and active filters live in the URL.

tasks.title: Draw the Epics KPI strip with now lists

tasks.title: Draw the lifecycle band with milestone axis

tasks.acceptance:
- stage cells come from the summary band; a stage filters the map by `epics[].status` of `tp epic export` and a phase opens Specs at it
- one milestone entry each: open or closed with what it waits on, gate members done of members, threshold written, absent, placeholder or met
- a Go test asserts the page reads the band and milestone-state fields

tasks.title: Draw the operator decision rows
tasks.description: Each operator decision with the command that settles it, every row from a payload.
tasks.acceptance:
- rows: actionable conditions, any-of groups as their choices, gates awaiting `--met`, a placeholder gate once with its `tp epic set` rewrite, run escalations from `--list`

tasks.title: Draw the plan review panel per slice
tasks.description: One row per slice: key, round with cap and grants, state, stale cause on hover, open by role, per-round counts as a small curve.
tasks.acceptance:

tasks.title: Draw the map from the exported layout
tasks.description: Epics placed by layout lanes, columns and rows; edges on selection, the critical path always.

tasks.title: Filter the map to one epic's neighbours

tasks.acceptance: - the filter keeps one epic, its dependencies and its dependents, marks each edge incoming or outgoing, and shows the edge's why on hover

tasks.title: Make the epic search accent-insensitive
tasks.description: Ids and titles matched ignoring case and diacritics, Turkish dotted and dotless i included.
tasks.acceptance:
- searching `isik` finds an epic whose id is `IŞIK-1`
- a Go test asserts the page's folding table maps ı, İ, ş, ğ, ç, ö and ü

tasks.title: Draw the epic drawer with its chain
tasks.description: Drawer with fields, dependencies, downstream, bound specs, stepper and history; the selected epic's chain and the milestone matrix.
tasks.acceptance:
- the drawer shows fields, dependencies with whys, downstream, bound specs with phase and loops, and its stepper (claim with author or skipped, bound, done); the chain panel shows every edge's why; the milestone matrix renders
- its history comes from the `--of-epic` GET, refetched on every push; an epic in no recorded slice says it has no graph history
- a hash-only round says no edge or why text was kept

tasks.title: Draw a slice's graph history between rounds
tasks.description: Per slice, its rounds with findings by role; between two chosen rounds, the snapshot diff beside the earlier round's findings.
tasks.acceptance:
- a slice's rounds in order with findings by role; choosing two rounds shows their diff with the earlier round's findings beside it
- fetched by GET when shown and again on every push

tasks.title: Draw the Specs tab from the list
tasks.description: Rows from tp export --list, grouped by phase in loop order.
tasks.acceptance:
- one row per task file: title and path, epic and its state, task progress, review and audit rounds, next step; grouped by phase in the loop's order, operator decisions first within a phase
- a filter, phase chips and an operator-decisions chip narrow it, `/` reaches the filter from anywhere, a row opens the Spec tab
- in tp's own repository every `spec/*.tasks.json` appears once, under the phase `tp resume <file>` reports

tasks.title: Draw the Spec tab header stepper
tasks.description: Stepper ground to release, release impact, and the tp resume command with a copy key.
tasks.acceptance:
- one stepper (ground, review, decompose, implement, audit, release), each step saying what happened or when it comes, the current marked, a pause mark where the operator decides
- a spec with review rounds and no tasks opens on Read with the step `tp resume` reports marked; one with tasks opens on Tasks
- the release impact from the summary and the `tp resume` command with a copy key

tasks.title: Draw the Spec tab Read view
tasks.description: The spec's text in anchored sections from tp export.
tasks.acceptance:
- the text in numbered sections with their `§N ¶M` anchors; a section's task count opens Tasks filtered to it
- an edit to spec text or a task's acceptance or description changes none of the pushed payloads: test editing the spec text with the tab open and decide whether waiting for the next push is acceptable; if not, add a per-file content hash to `tp export --list` (with its test) so the page refetches

tasks.title: Draw the Spec tab Tasks view
tasks.description: Steps and Board in one panel, beside a progress or task panel that never closes.
tasks.acceptance:
- Steps puts each task one step below the last task it waits on; Board has ready, in progress, waiting, done, its counts equal to `tp status`'s open, wip and done
- with no task picked the side panel shows progress: tasks by state, estimate left, running tasks against estimate, tasks closed over time
- with a task picked it shows state, time against estimate or evidence and commit, acceptance, dependencies, its section and its command

tasks.title: Draw the Spec tab History view
tasks.description: Rounds on a time axis, the round table and each review round's snapshot diff.
tasks.acceptance:
- rounds on a time axis and the round table: findings or FAIL count, clean, cap, streak
- each review round's snapshot diff from the round before beside its findings; a spec with two review rounds shows the diff of `snapshot-round-1.md` and `snapshot-round-2.md`

tasks.title: Draw the lifecycle-over-time chart
tasks.description: Work epics per stage per day from the summary series.
tasks.acceptance:
- the chart draws the summary's per-day series; an unknown binding time shows as unknown, never on a guessed day
- its ⓘ says an epic's planning time is not recorded, so a later-added epic counts as planned from the first day
